The Premier League's first season was 1992/93, with 22 clubs. It dropped to 20 in 1995/96.
Brian Deane scored the first ever Premier League goal, for Sheffield United against Manchester United on 15 August 1992.
Alan Shearer is the Premier League's all-time top scorer with 260 goals.
Harry Kane scored 213 Premier League goals for Spurs before joining Bayern Munich in 2023.
Arsenal went the whole 2003/04 league season unbeaten: 26 wins and 12 draws.
Arsenal's 49-game unbeaten league run finally ended at Old Trafford in October 2004.
Manchester City's 100 points in 2017/18 is the Premier League record.
Manchester City scored 106 league goals in 2017/18, a Premier League record.
Manchester City won 18 league games in a row during their 100-point season in 2017/18.
Leicester City won the 2015/16 title after starting the season as 5000-1 outsiders.
Jamie Vardy scored in 11 Premier League games in a row in 2015, a record.
Erling Haaland scored 36 league goals in 2022/23, the most in a Premier League season.
Before Haaland, the season record was 34 goals, shared by Andy Cole (1993/94) and Alan Shearer (1994/95), both in 42-game seasons.
Mohamed Salah scored 32 league goals in 2017/18, a record for a 38-game season at the time.
Manchester City won four Premier League titles in a row from 2020/21 to 2023/24, the first club to do it.
Sadio Mané scored the fastest Premier League hat-trick: 2 minutes 56 seconds, for Southampton against Aston Villa in May 2015.
Robbie Fowler's 4 minute 33 second hat-trick against Arsenal in 1994 was the fastest until Sadio Mané came along.
Shane Long scored the fastest Premier League goal: 7.69 seconds, for Southampton at Watford in April 2019.
Derby County's 11 points in 2007/08 is the lowest total in Premier League history.
Petr Čech kept 202 Premier League clean sheets, the most ever.
Chelsea conceded just 15 league goals in 2004/05, a Premier League record.
Edwin van der Sar went 1,311 minutes without conceding a Premier League goal in 2008/09.
Sir Alex Ferguson won 13 Premier League titles with Manchester United.
Ryan Giggs won 13 Premier League titles, more than any other player.
Ryan Giggs scored in each of the Premier League's first 21 seasons.
Ryan Giggs has the most assists in Premier League history, with 162.
Kevin De Bruyne's 20 assists in 2019/20 equalled Thierry Henry's single-season record from 2002/03.
Thierry Henry won the Premier League Golden Boot four times: 2002, 2004, 2005 and 2006.
Cristiano Ronaldo won the 2007/08 Golden Boot with 31 league goals.
Andy Cole was the first player to score five in a Premier League game, in Manchester United's 9-0 win over Ipswich in March 1995.
Jermain Defoe scored five times in Tottenham's 9-1 win over Wigan in November 2009.
Liverpool beat Bournemouth 9-0 in August 2022, equalling the biggest winning margin in Premier League history.
Portsmouth 7-4 Reading in September 2007 is the highest-scoring game in Premier League history: 11 goals.
Ole Gunnar Solskjær came off the bench to score four in Manchester United's 8-1 win at Nottingham Forest in 1999.
Jermain Defoe scored 24 Premier League goals as a substitute, the most ever.
Peter Crouch scored 53 Premier League headers, the most in the competition's history.
Frank Lampard scored 177 Premier League goals, the most by a midfielder.
Craig Bellamy played for seven Premier League clubs and scored for all seven.
Arsène Wenger managed Arsenal in 828 Premier League games.
Liverpool won the 2019/20 title with seven games to spare, the earliest finish ever. It was their first league title in 30 years.
Blackburn Rovers won the Premier League in 1994/95, with Alan Shearer scoring 34 goals.
Up to 2024/25, only seven clubs had won the Premier League: Manchester United, Blackburn, Arsenal, Chelsea, Manchester City, Leicester and Liverpool.
Swansea became the first Welsh club in the Premier League in 2011.
Brentford played their first ever Premier League season in 2021/22.
Steven Gerrard played 504 Premier League games for Liverpool but never won the title.
Les Ferdinand scored the Premier League's 10,000th goal in December 2001.
Marc Albrighton scored the Premier League's 20,000th goal, for Aston Villa, in December 2011.
